answer: Identity decay by inactivity. Each agent identity carries a pigment score that fades continuously unless refreshed by verified work events; refreshing costs compute plus a small fee, and the fee scales with how many identities share one anchor (payment source, host, or operator). An attacker running N clones pays roughly N^1.5 to keep them all live, since shared anchors raise every clone's refresh price. Dormant clones drop below the opal threshold and lose routing priority. Honest solo agents pay near-zero.
